blocks.text: The greenhouse effect is the natural process in which gases in the Earth's atmosphere, greenhouse gases (GHGs), trap the heat radiated from the Earth's surface: they let sunlight pass but stop heat escaping directly into space, keeping the Earth warm enough for life.

The concentrations of these gases, especially CO2, have risen markedly, mainly through the use of fossil fuels to run machines, drive vehicles, heat homes and generate electricity. The resulting enhanced, unnatural warming of the atmosphere is the major negative impact of human activities on the environment.

blocks.alt: Two panels. Natural greenhouse effect: sunlight passes through a thin layer of greenhouse gases to the Earth's surface; heat radiated back is partly trapped and partly escapes in three arrows. Enhanced greenhouse effect: the gas layer is thicker (more CO2, CH4, N2O), more heat is trapped and only one arrow of heat escapes.
blocks.caption: Natural and enhanced greenhouse effect (original diagram after Figure 25.9).
blocks.long_description: Greenhouse gases in the atmosphere let sunlight through but trap part of the heat radiated from the Earth's surface, keeping the planet warm enough for life: the natural greenhouse effect. Burning fossil fuels for machines, vehicles, heating and electricity, and deforestation, have raised the concentrations of these gases, especially carbon dioxide; the thicker blanket traps more heat, causing the enhanced, unnatural warming of the atmosphere known as global warming.

blocks.title: Tidbits
blocks.text: According to the World Meteorological Organization, as the book reports, CO2 was about 280 parts per million before industrialisation and reached 428 ppm in 2026, still rising; the mean global temperature has risen about 1 C since 1900. Pakistan contributes less than 1% of global greenhouse emissions but is ranked among the ten countries most vulnerable to climate change.

blocks.prompt: Without any greenhouse effect, what would happen to the Earth?
blocks.explanation: Heat would escape directly into space and the Earth would be too cold to support life as we know it; the problem is the enhanced effect, not the natural one.

items: Natural greenhouse effect keeps Earth warm enough for life.
Extra CO2 from fossil fuels and deforestation enhances it, causing global warming.
